title: Help yourself!
paragraphs: I need help! I have to fix a leaking pipe in my bathroom but I’m not sure where to begin. I know I lack the necessary DIY skills, but luckily there are numerous books and online videos that will hopefully give me the information I need.
Publications that help us to help ourselves are nothing new, but the range of them is increasing with advice being given far beyond practical tasks around the house.

Bookshops these days are full of titles which claim to boost your self-confidence, your wealth, your love life or your career. Some claim to improve your life within seven days! It‘s big business and it’s thought that the self-help industry is worth $10bn in the US alone.

The first self-help book called ‘How to Win Friends and Influence People‘ was published in 1936, and has since sold 30 million copies and is still popular now. It includes guidance on how to make people like you and how to make your life happier. It might seem strange to think that we need a book to tell us how to live our lives but self-help books remain a go-to remedy for those of us looking for enlightenment.

There are, of course, trends in what we need help with. Emma Marshall, who works at British bookshop Waterstones, says “at the moment we’re in the tidying up, getting rid of things trend... I think the trend right now is about slowing down in your life.” It seems there is always something we need help with, and reading about it can be very therapeutic - it makes us feel good, even if we don‘t do anything about it.

Of course, the internet has become the place to go to for salvation. We’ve got used to searching for solutions online, and now these solutions even include how to fix or improve our lives. Interestingly, psychologist Caroline Beaton, says people called ‘millennials‘ are self-critical — they are aware of their own faults — which also means they’re more likely to spend time and money on self-help. There‘s also a theory that the self-help industry does well during a recession — people are perhaps even more likely to reach for self-help to improve their situation.

Whatever the reason for the continued interest in self-help, it’s good to know help is at hand when we need it. The alternative to finding a happier life is just to come to terms with yourself as you are - I know, I read about it in a book! Do you believe in self-help books?

vocabulary.entry: leaking [adj.] /ˈliːkɪŋ/ 渗漏的；泄漏的
vocabulary.example: The leaking pipe caused water damage to the floor.
vocabulary.translation: 漏水的水管对地板造成了水损。

vocabulary.entry: DIY [n.] /ˌdiː aɪ ˈwaɪ/ 自己动手做 (Do It Yourself的缩写)
vocabulary.example: He enjoys DIY projects like building furniture.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢像制作家具这样的自己动手项目。

vocabulary.entry: numerous [adj.] /ˈnjuːmərəs/ 众多的；许多的
vocabulary.example: She has received numerous awards for her work.
vocabulary.translation: 她的工作获得了无数奖项。

vocabulary.entry: publications [n. pl.] /ˌpʌblɪˈkeɪʃənz/ 出版物 (单数: publication)
vocabulary.example: The library has a wide range of scientific publications.
vocabulary.translation: 这家图书馆有各种各样的科学出版物。

vocabulary.entry: boost [v.] /buːst/ 促进；增加；提高
vocabulary.example: Getting a good grade boosted his confidence.
vocabulary.translation: 取得好成绩增强了他的信心。

vocabulary.entry: guidance [n.] /ˈɡaɪdəns/ 指导；引导
vocabulary.example: Students need guidance when choosing a career.
vocabulary.translation: 学生在选择职业时需要指导。

vocabulary.entry: go-to [adj.] /ˈɡəʊ tuː/ 首选的；可信赖的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: This café is my go-to place for lunch.
vocabulary.translation: 这家咖啡馆是我吃午餐的首选之地。

vocabulary.entry: remedy [n.] /ˈremədi/ 解决办法；疗法
vocabulary.example: The best remedy for stress is exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 缓解压力的最佳方法是锻炼。

vocabulary.entry: enlightenment [n.] /ɪnˈlaɪtənmənt/ 启迪；启蒙
vocabulary.example: The book provided her with spiritual enlightenment.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书给了她精神上的启迪。

vocabulary.entry: trends [n. pl.] /trendz/ 趋势；潮流 (单数: trend)
vocabulary.example: Fashion trends change every season.
vocabulary.translation: 时尚潮流每季都在变化。

vocabulary.entry: tidying up [phr.] /ˈtaɪdiɪŋ ʌp/ 整理；收拾
vocabulary.example: Tidying up your desk can help you focus better.
vocabulary.translation: 整理你的书桌可以帮助你更好地集中注意力。

vocabulary.entry: getting rid of [phr.] /ˈɡetɪŋ rɪd əv/ 摆脱；处理掉
vocabulary.example: Getting rid of clutter can reduce stress.
vocabulary.translation: 处理掉杂物可以减轻压力。

vocabulary.entry: slowing down [phr.] /ˈsləʊɪŋ daʊn/ 放慢速度；慢下来
vocabulary.example: Slowing down and relaxing is important for mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 放慢节奏和放松对心理健康很重要。

vocabulary.entry: therapeutic [adj.] /ˌθerəˈpjuːtɪk/ 有疗效的；有益于身心健康的
vocabulary.example: Gardening can be very therapeutic.
vocabulary.translation: 园艺可能非常有疗效。

vocabulary.entry: salvation [n.] /sælˈveɪʃən/ 拯救；救星
vocabulary.example: The new medicine was a salvation for many patients.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新药是许多病人的救星。

vocabulary.entry: millennials [n. pl.] /mɪˈleniəlz/ 千禧一代 (单数: millennial)
vocabulary.example: Millennials grew up with the internet and smartphones.
vocabulary.translation: 千禧一代是伴随着互联网和智能手机成长起来的。

vocabulary.entry: self-critical [adj.] /ˌself ˈkrɪtɪkəl/ 自我批评的；善于自我反省的
vocabulary.example: Being self-critical can help you improve.
vocabulary.translation: 善于自我批评可以帮助你进步。

vocabulary.entry: recession [n.] /rɪˈseʃən/ 经济衰退；不景气
vocabulary.example: Many people lost their jobs during the recession.
vocabulary.translation: 经济衰退期间许多人失去了工作。

vocabulary.entry: alternative [n.] /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ 可供选择的事物
vocabulary.example: We need to find an alternative to plastic bags.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要找到塑料袋的替代品。

vocabulary.entry: come to terms with [phr.] /kʌm tə tɜːmz wɪð/ 接受；妥协
vocabulary.example: It took him years to come to terms with his loss.
vocabulary.translation: 他花了好几年才接受自己的损失。
